question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.**
solution:
The correct answer is **'towards'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given blank needs a **preposition **to show the relationship between the novelists' attitudes toward their subject. 
 
• Let us look into the usage of the given options (all of which are prepositions) - 
 
 
• **despite - **without being affected by; in spite of.
 
• **under - **extending or directly below.
 
• **through - **moving in one side and out of the other side of (an opening, channel, or location).
 
• **towards - **expressing the relation between behavior or an attitude and the person or thing at which it is directed or with which it is concerned.
 
 
 
• From the above-listed usage, we can conclude that **towards **is the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
 
• Hence, **option 4 **is the correct answer. 

**Correct passage__ - ***Novelists when they write novels, tend to take an almost god-like attitude (1) **__towards__ **their subject, pretending to have a total comprehension of the story, a man's life, (2) __**which**__ they can therefore recount as God Himself might, nothing standing between them and the naked truth, the entire story meaningful in (3) **__every__** detail. I am as little able to do this as the novelist is, even though my story is more important to me than any novelist's is to him – for this is my story; it is the story of a man, not of an invented or possible, or idealized or otherwise (4) __**absent**__ figure, but of a unique (5) __**being**__ of flesh and blood. *
